title: CHAPTER 3: CELL DIVISION – MITOSIS AND MEIOSIS

blocks.content: 1. Cell Division – Meaning

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The cell cycle consists of Interphase (G1, S, G2 phases) and the M-phase (Mitosis/Meiosis).
DNA replication occurs exclusively during the S-phase (Synthesis phase) of Interphase.
Mitosis is an equational division resulting in two genetically identical diploid daughter cells used for growth and repair.
Meiosis is a reductional division producing four non-identical haploid gametes for sexual reproduction.
Crossing over occurs during the Pachytene stage of Prophase I in Meiosis, driving genetic recombination.

blocks.content:
Cell division is the process by which a parent cell divides into two or more daughter cells.

It is essential for growth, repair, reproduction, and continuity of life.

In unicellular organisms, cell division itself acts as a mode of reproduction.

In multicellular organisms, cell division helps in growth and replacement of damaged or worn-out cells.

Cell division ensures proper distribution of genetic material.

It occurs in a regulated manner to maintain genetic stability.
2. Cell Cycle

The cell cycle is the series of events that take place in a cell leading to its division.

It has two main phases: Interphase and Mitotic phase.

Interphase includes G1 phase, S phase, and G2 phase.

DNA replication occurs during S phase.

Interphase is the longest phase of the cell cycle.

The mitotic phase includes nuclear division and cytokinesis.
3. Types of Cell Division

There are two main types of cell division: Mitosis and Meiosis.

Mitosis occurs in somatic cells.

Meiosis occurs in germ cells.

Mitosis maintains chromosome number.

Meiosis reduces chromosome number by half.

Both are essential for survival and reproduction.
CHAPTER 3: CELL DIVISION – MITOSIS AND MEIOSIS
4. Mitosis – Definition

Mitosis is an equational division in which a parent cell divides into two identical daughter cells.

The chromosome number remains unchanged.

It occurs in body cells.

Mitosis is essential for growth, repair, and asexual reproduction.

It ensures equal distribution of chromosomes.
5. Stages of Mitosis

Mitosis occurs in four stages: Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, and Telophase.

Prophase: Chromosomes condense and nuclear membrane disappears.

Metaphase: Chromosomes align at equator.

Anaphase: Sister chromatids separate.

Telophase: Nuclear membrane reforms.

Cytokinesis follows mitosis.
6. Significance of Mitosis

Mitosis helps in growth and development.

It repairs damaged tissues.

It maintains chromosome number.

It plays role in asexual reproduction.

Abnormal mitosis can cause cancer.
7. Meiosis – Definition

Meiosis is a reduction division producing four haploid cells.

It occurs in reproductive organs.

Meiosis introduces variation.

It halves chromosome number.

It is essential for sexual reproduction.
8. Stages of Meiosis

Meiosis occurs in two stages: Meiosis I and Meiosis II.

Meiosis I includes Prophase I, Metaphase I, Anaphase I, Telophase I.

Crossing over occurs in Prophase I.

Meiosis II is similar to mitosis.

Four haploid cells are formed.

items: DNA replication happens in the S-phase of Interphase, NOT during Mitosis or Meiosis itself.
Crossing over and chiasmata formation occur specifically during Prophase I (Pachytene stage) of Meiosis I.
Mitosis is referred to as equational division, whereas Meiosis I is reductional division.
Chromosomes align along the metaphase plate at the equator during Metaphase.

blocks.content: 9. Significance of Meiosis

Meiosis produces gametes.

It introduces genetic variation.

It maintains chromosome number in species.

Errors in meiosis cause genetic disorders.
10. IMPORTANT FACTS –  FOCUS

• Mitosis is equational division.

• Meiosis is reduction division.

• PMAT are stages of mitosis.

• Crossing over occurs in Prophase I.

• Meiosis produces four haploid cells.

• Mitosis produces two diploid cells.

• Meiosis occurs in germ cells.

• Mitosis occurs in somatic cells.

• Errors in cell division can cause cancer.
